verses.text: Dead flies can make a perfumer's oil stink. That's how a little foolishness can outweigh wisdom and honor.
A wise person's heart leans to the right. A fool's heart leans to the left.
A fool can be walking down the road, run out of sense entirely, and show everybody what a fool they are.
If a ruler gets angry at you, stay where you are. A gentle response can put even serious offenses to rest.
I've seen something wrong under the sun, the kind of mistake that comes from the ruler.
Foolishness gets a seat of honor, while rich people are made to sit down low.
I've seen servants riding horses and princes walking on the ground like servants.
Dig a pit and you might fall into it. Break through a wall and a snake might bite you.
Cut stones out and they can hurt you. Split wood and you can get hurt doing that too.
A dull ax takes more muscle if you don't sharpen it. Skill gets the job done.
If the snake bites before you charm it, what good were the charmer's words?
Wise people speak with grace. A fool's own words swallow them up.
Their talk starts off foolish and ends up in harmful madness.
A fool keeps piling on words. Nobody knows what's coming. Who can tell anyone what will happen after they're gone?
Work wears fools out. They don't even know the way into town.
What trouble for a country whose king is a child and whose rulers start feasting in the morning!
Happy is the land whose king comes from nobles and whose rulers eat at the proper time to get their strength up, without getting drunk.
Get lazy and the roof sags. Keep your hands idle and the house starts leaking.
People throw a feast to laugh, wine brings cheer to life, and money pays for it all.
Don't curse the king, even in your head. Don't curse rich people in your bedroom. A bird might carry your words, and something with wings could spread the story.
